chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Whoever kills a believer intentionally is subject to retaliation (qisas), unless the heirs of the slain agree to accept the blood money (diyah) or agree to a sum greater or lesser than the standard blood money. If they do so among themselves, it is valid; if they do not agree, retaliation is executed.

And he said: The blood money is ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels. As for what the preceding narrations contained regarding that one hundred and twenty dirhams are extracted from each camel.

key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: Ten thousand dirhams (standard currency unit for diyah)
key_terms.قِيَاد: Retaliation (Qisas), specifically in the context of murder
key_terms.مِائَةٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ: One hundred camels (livestock unit for diyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for intentional murder and how is blood money calculated?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the flexibility of qisas, emphasizing that the victim's heirs hold the discretionary power to accept diyah or agree to a mutually adjusted amount, whether higher or lower than the standard. It explicitly defines the baseline diyah as ten thousand dirhams or one thousand dinars, while noting the scholarly tradition of deriving specific livestock valuations (120 dirhams per camel) from other narrations. This highlights the Shia juristic view of diyah as a compensatory right of the heirs rather than a fixed state penalty.
